title: Eva Marie Saint’s stolen glances
gist: David Thomson's tribute to Eva Marie Saint, who died at 102, argues that her role as Eve Kendall in Hitchcock's North by Northwest (1959) was inspired casting against type. He reads the film as a work of veiled eroticism that slipped past censors and reflects Hitchcock's mix of adoration for women and a need to punish them, and calls the rest of her long career exemplary but uninteresting.

insights.claim: Casting Eva Marie Saint, known for a pale, quiet, virtuous persona, as the two-faced seductress Eve Kendall in North by Northwest was a deliberate play against type that Thomson thinks the film industry found baffling.
insights.so_what: Counter-intuitive casting can create enduring cultural value, a recurring lesson for studios and content producers.
insights.quote: With an actress so unlikely that the business must have wondered, ‘Why would Hitch cast her?’
insights.locator: So the meeting on the train
insights.speaker: David Thomson

insights.claim: Thomson argues that North by Northwest rests on both Hitchcock's adoration of women and his secretive need to punish them for being attractive to him, with Eve Kendall as his most provocative and veiled goddess.
insights.so_what: Shows how auteur psychology shapes lasting cultural products, with little direct market relevance.
insights.quote: North by Northwest hangs on not just Hitch’s adoration of women, but his secretive need to punish them for being so attractive to him
insights.speaker: David Thomson

insights.claim: In 1959 Hollywood, respectable, sophisticated entertainments could be casually erotic through innuendo and distancing, so much so that censors effectively missed it.
insights.so_what: Content restrictions tend to push creators toward subtext rather than remove the material, a pattern relevant to today's content moderation debates.
insights.quote: respectable, sophisticated entertainments could be so casually erotic that the so-called censors might have been retired as deaf and blind
insights.speaker: David Thomson

insights.claim: Eva Marie Saint worked into the 21st century with around a hundred credits and won a supporting actress Oscar for On the Waterfront, but Thomson judges the full list exemplary, professional and uninteresting next to North by Northwest.
insights.so_what: One defining role can outweigh a whole career in cultural memory, which matters for how film libraries are valued.
insights.quote: The full list makes it hard to see her career as anything other than exemplary, professional, and uninteresting.
insights.speaker: David Thomson
